A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Editable Concept Bottleneck Models and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The shared methods and experiments can be matched reliably across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original OAI/CUB F1 scores and runtimes, editing-ratio experiments, concept-removal analyses, and visualization results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds CelebA evaluations, a CUB membership-inference experiment, and additional concept-influence visualizations.

M1.justification: The main editing formulas and architecture are retained. However, v1 Algorithm 5 computes concept-level curvature over retained concepts, whereas v2 Algorithm 7 invokes Algorithm 4, whose loss sums over all concepts. Theorem 4.3 still specifies retained concepts. Whether this represents a procedure change or an omission during pseudocode refactoring is unresolved.

E1.justification: v2 adds CelebA face-attribute prediction to the retained medical-image and bird-classification coverage. Section 5.1 assigns eight attributes as labels and the remaining 32 as concepts, and Table 1 evaluates all three editing levels on this additional domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 2 retain Retrain, CBM-IF, and ECBM; Figure 3 retains Retrain versus ECBM. CelebA uses the same comparator set. Membership inference supplies an evaluation tool, not an additional competing editing method.

E3.justification: v2 adds a distinct removal-verification protocol: RMIA scores before and after editing 200 CUB training members, compared with 200 test non-members. It also specifies CelebA's eight-label/32-concept construction. The original OAI/CUB editing rates, deletion sweeps, F1 metric, and runtime evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new membership-inference diagnostic tests whether removed samples become less distinguishable from non-members. Appendix G.2 also adds per-image concept-label influence analyses for CUB and OAI in Figures 8–12. The existing editing-ratio sweeps and most/least-influential-concept removal analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 4 adds Gaussian score-distribution curves, and Appendix G.1 introduces a likelihood model parameterized by means and variances. The existing five/ten repetition information and Table 1's plus/minus reporting practice are unchanged. No increased run count, significance test, or uncertainty interval for the new membership results is reported.

E6.justification: Original OAI/CUB table values and plots are retained. New CelebA concept-label results include ECBM F1 0.3845 and runtime 15.67 seconds versus Retrain 0.3827 and 57.60 seconds. The new CUB experiment reports mean RMIA decreasing from 0.063505 to 0.052105 after editing, versus 0.049465 for non-members. Appendix influence-score entries are also added.

T1.justification: v2 revises the influence-function perturbation definition and adds Appendix A's Taylor derivation under strong convexity. The CBM-specific theorems and proofs are retained. The new derivation introduces sign/scaling inconsistencies, including a positive influence term for deletion where v1 Section 3 uses its negative.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims: three levels of editable CBMs, influence-function approximations avoiding retraining, EK-FAC acceleration, and efficient, effective editing. The added experiments support these existing claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the RMIA shift as evidence of reduced membership vulnerability and removal of training-sample influence, an interpretation absent from v1. The explicit limitations paragraph is removed, although the approximation nature of ECBM remains acknowledged elsewhere.

D1.justification: v2 documents CelebA's attribute allocation and RMIA's use of logits and Gaussian likelihood parameters. Shared EK-FAC routines replace repeated pseudocode, making some case-specific loss restrictions less explicit. Hardware and backbone disclosures are retained; detailed attack estimation procedures and CelebA's concept-deletion count remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Concept Embedding Models, CelebA, and the membership-inference works of Shokri et al. and Zarifzadeh et al. The principal novelty positioning remains unchanged. The additional Sheth/Kahou bibliography entry duplicates an already cited work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. Changes include localized wording edits, updated authorship, author-year citations, appendix reorganization, and consolidation of EK-FAC pseudocode. Some duplicated numerical text is introduced, including '11-1010' in the Figure 3 discussion.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains CelebA columns, Figure 4 adds paired membership-score histograms, and Figures 8–12 introduce per-image influence-score displays. Original Figures 4–6 are retained as Figures 5–7. The document template, headers, and algorithm displays are also reformatted.

improvement.justification: The CelebA results and membership-inference diagnostic broaden empirical support and partially address v1's limited direct validation of data removal. The gain is modest: new experimental details remain incomplete, and the added derivation and refactored pseudocode introduce inconsistencies. The core results and CBM proofs are retained.
